title: Finland – Software package and information systems – Family Pedigree Software Solution
description: The HUS Group requests tenders for family pedigree software solution mainly for the Clinical Genetics Unit. The procured software must be an on-premises, ready-to-use solution installed and operated within HUS-managed infrastructure and environment. The scope of the procurement includes software licences, implementation services, and related maintenance and support services required for the operational use of the software. The software will be used on a daily basis by approximately 20 to 30 users mainly within the Clinical Genetics Unit, including both physicians and nurses. In addition, a small number of users from the cardiology specialty will use the system. The family pedigree software is a critical tool in the Clinical Genetics Unit's daily operations. Information concerning almost all patients and families treated by the unit is recorded in the software. The Clinical Genetics Unit receives approximately 150 to 200 patient visits per week. The information stored in the software is of long-term clinical significance. When new patients from previously recorded families contact the Clinical Genetics Unit, often after several years, access to historical family data is essential. Therefore, reliable data preservation, availability, and retrievability are key requirements of the procurement. Laboratory system integration may be procured as an optional service and implemented as separately ordered expert work at the hourly expert rates specified in the Pricing Appendix. The subject matter and requirements of the procurement are described in detail in the call for tenders and its appendices.

description: Obiectul acestui contract îl reprezintă achiziția publică de servicii de proiectare, asistență tehnică din partea proiectantului pe parcursul execuției lucrărilor și execuție lucrări aferente obiectivului de investitii “CENTRU MULTIMODAL AUTOBUZE ELECTRICE”, oraș Chitila, județ Ilfov de către personal autorizat, in conformitate cu prevederile documentatiei de atribuire. Obiectivul de investitii “CENTRU MULTIMODAL AUTOBUZE ELECTRICE”, oraș Chitila, județ Ilfov”, SMIS 353265, finantata prin PR 2021-2027, are un caracter integrat cu proiectele de achiziție mijloace de transport în comun (autobuze electrice) derulate în prezent de UAT Oraș Chitila iar prin realizarea investiției “CENTRU MULTIMODAL AUTOBUZE ELECTRICE”, oraș Chitila, județ Ilfov”, SMIS 353265, se va asigura funcționarea adecvată a mijloacelor de transport în comun nou achiziționate. Obiectivul general al proiectului este îmbunătățirea și modernizarea infrastructurii dedicate transportului public urban ecologic, prin realizarea unei autobaze pentru vehicule electrice în orașul Chitila, județul Ilfov, cu scopul de a sprijini tranziția către un transport sustenabil și eficient energetic. Realizarea obiectivului general – construirea și operaționalizarea Centrului multimodal pentru autobuze electrice din Chitila – presupune atingerea următoarelor obiective specifice, fiecare corelat cu un rezultat concret și măsurabil. OBS 1: Realizarea unei autobaze complet echipate pentru găzduirea, întreținerea și operarea a minimum 21 de autobuze electrice în orașul Chitila. OBS 2. Creșterea gradului de utilizare a transportului public ecologic prin atragerea unui număr mai mare de călători, ca urmare a îmbunătățirii condițiilor de transport oferite de autobuzele electrice. OBS 3: Reducerea impactului asupra mediului prin sprijinirea operării transportului public cu emisii zero în orașul Chitila și creșterea atractivității utilizării transportului în comun. Aceste obiective au următoarele rezultate: R1: Autobaza construită și funcțională, cu o capacitate de operare pentru minimum 21 de autobuze electrice. R2: Facilități auxiliare operaționale in cadrul autobazei: clădire dispecerat, zone de parcare, zone tehnice, spălătorie, rampe de inspecţie etc. R3: Creșterea cu minimum 0,16% a numărului de utilizatori în primul an de operare a noii autobaze (4852244 utilizatori anuali ai transporturilor publice noi sau modernizate în primul an de operare a autobazei nou construit). R4: Scădere a emisiilor GES cu minimum 4567 tone CO2 echivalent/an ca urmare a operării autobuzelor electrice găzduite de autobaza nou construită. Orice operator economic interesat are dreptul de a solicita clarificări/informații suplimentare în legătură cu documentația de atribuire până în a 18-a zi înainte de termenul limită de depunere a ofertelor. Autoritatea contractantă va răspunde în mod clar și complet tuturor solicitărilor de clarificări/informații suplimentare în legatură cu documentația de atribuire în a 11-a zi inainte de data limită de depunere a ofertelor. Autoritatea contractantă nu va răspunde la solicitările de clarificări transmise după data limită stabilită. Orice solicitare de clarificări trebuie transmisă în SEAP, semnată cu semnatură electronică extinsă, bazată pe un certificat calificat, eliberat de un furnizor de servicii de certificare acreditat.

title: Canadian Macroeconomic Data
description: Title: Canadian Macroeconomic Data 1. Advance Contract Award Notice (ACAN) An ACAN is a public notice indicating to the supplier community that a department or agency intends to award a contract for goods, services or construction to a pre-identified supplier, thereby allowing other suppliers to signal their interest in bidding, by submitting a statement of capabilities. If no supplier submits a statement of capabilities that meets the requirements set out in the ACAN, on or before the closing date stated in the ACAN, the contracting officer may then proceed with the award to the pre-identified supplier. 2. Definition of the requirement The Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions Canada (OSFI) has a requirement for a subscription to access curated Canadian macroeconomic data covering national, provincial, and regional economies, and Canadian Real Estate Association (CREA) data, delivered via an application program interface (API). The purpose of this Advance Contract Award Notice (ACAN) is to signal the government's intention to award a contract for these services to Haver Analytics. Before awarding a contract, however, the government would like to provide other suppliers with the opportunity to demonstrate that they are capable of satisfying the requirements set out in this Notice, by submitting a statement of capabilities during the 15 calendar day posting period. If other potential suppliers submit a statement of capabilities during the 15 calendar day posting period that meet the requirements set out in the ACAN, the government will proceed to a full tendering process on either the government's electronic tendering service or through traditional means, in order to award the contract. If no other supplier submits, on or before the closing date, a statement of capabilities meeting the requirements set out in the ACAN, a contract will be awarded to the pre-selected supplier. 3. Criteria for assessment of the Statement of Capabilities (Minimum Essential Requirements) Any interested supplier must demonstrate by way of a statement of capabilities that it meets the following requirements: • Ability to Provide comprehensive Canadian macroeconomic and financial data covering, at a minimum, national accounts, employment and labour market statistics, inflation and interest rates, monetary and credit aggregates, government finance statistics, business and consumer activity indicators, population and demographic statistics, other major economic indicators required for economic forecasting and financial stability assessment. Data shall include lengthy historical time series (50+ years where data exists) and ongoing updates from official Canadian statistical agencies, central banks and other recognized sources. • Provide regional and sub-national economic data covering Canadian provinces, territories and major metropolitan covering, at a minimum, employment and labour market statistics, population and migration data, housing and construction indicators, income and consumption measures, prices and inflation indicators where available, regional economic activity and business indicators, and other regional economic indicators required for regional economic analysis and forecasting. Data shall include lengthy historical time series (50+ years where data exists) and ongoing updates from official Canadian statistical agencies, central banks and other recognized sources. • Provide Canadian residential real estate market information, including home sales activity, prices and price indices, housing inventory and listings, market supply and demand indicators, and other housing market indicators relevant to real estate analysis and financial system monitoring. Data shall include lengthy historical time series (50+ years where data exists) and be provided at varying levels including national, provincial and metropolitan areas. • Provide access to a software platform and/or web-based interface for searching, extracting, visualizing, transforming, and downloading data while maintaining data export functionality compatible with common analytical applications • Provide enterprise-wide license available for all OSFI users • Provide Documentation, training materials and user guides, as well as offer technical support, maintenance services, product updates and software enhancements (as applicable) • Provide programmatic access to subscribed datasets through a modern application programming interface (API) that supports automated retrieval of time-series data, metadata access and search functionality, bulk data extraction capabilities, standard authentication and security protocols, integration with statistical analytical and forecasting software, and machine-readable output formats such as JSON, CML, CSV or equivalent. 4. Applicability of the trade agreement(s) to the procurement This procurement is not subject to the following trade agreement(s) • Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA) • Revised World Trade Organization - Agreement on Government Procurement (WTO-AGP) • Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) • Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP) • Canada-Chile Free Trade Agreement (CCFTA) • Canada-Colombia Free Trade Agreement • Canada-Honduras Free Trade Agreement • Canada-Korea Free Trade Agreement • Canada-Panama Free Trade Agreement • Canada-Peru Free Trade Agreement (CPFTA) • Canada-United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement (Canada-UK TCA) • Canada-Ukraine Free Trade Agreement (CUFTA) 5. Justification for the Pre-Selected Supplier Haver Analytics maintains exclusive ownership of curated macroeconomic and financial data products, including its user interface and analytical tools, proprietary data structures, series identifiers, concordance tables, historical vintages, and delivery formats. These elements are unique to Haver and are not reproduced or licensed through third party distributors. 6. Government Contracts Regulations Exception(s) The following exception to the Government Contracts Regulations is invoked for this procurement under subsection 6(d) - "only one person is capable of performing the work". 7. Ownership of Intellectual Property Ownership of any Foreground Intellectual Property arising out of the proposed contract will vest in the Contractor. 8. Period of the proposed contract or delivery date The proposed contract is for a period of one (1) year, with three (3) options to extend the contract for up to a period of one (1) year. 9. Cost estimate of the proposed contract The estimated value of the contract, including the option periods, is $46,559 USD 10. Name and address of the pre-identified supplier Haver Analytics 60 E 42nd St #3310 New York, NY 10165 United States 11. Suppliers' right to submit a statement of capabilities Suppliers who consider themselves fully qualified and available to meet the specified requirements may submit a statement of capabilities in writing to the Contracting Authority identified in this Notice on or before the closing date of this Notice. The statement of capabilities must clearly demonstrate how the supplier meets the advertised requirements. 12. Closing date for a submission of a statement of capabilities The closing date and time for acceptance of Statements of Capabilities is October 8, 2026 at 2:00 pm (EDT). 13. Inquiries and submission of statements of capabilities Inquiries and statements of capabilities are to be directed to: Cameron Marchand Senior Contracting Officer e-mail: contracting-approvisionnement@osfi-bsif.gc.ca 255 Albert St. 12th floor Ottawa, Ontario K1A 0H2

title: Specialized Vehicle Upfitting Services
description: Advance Contract Award Notice Definition of ACAN An Advance Contract Award Notice (ACAN) is a public notice informing suppliers that Canada intends to award a contract for goods, services or construction to a pre-identified supplier, and invites other suppliers to express their interest by submitting a statement of capabilities. If no other supplier submits a statement of capabilities demonstrating how they meet the set requirements in the ACAN by the closing date stated in the ACAN, the buyer may then proceed with the award to the pre-identified supplier. Purpose of the ACAN The purpose of this Advance Contract Award Notice (ACAN) is to signal the Royal Canadian Mounted Police’s intention to award a contract for Specialized Vehicle Upfitting Services to Battleshield Industries Limited, as the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) believes this is the only supplier capable of providing all of the services within the National Capital Region, as set out in this Notice. Requirement description The Royal Canadian Mounted Police, Communication Security (COMSEC) has a requirement for Specialized Upfitting services for a vehicle, that will enable the RCMP to rapidly deploy a fully equipped mobile COMSEC Suite capable of processing high volumes of information efficiently. The work will involve the following tasks: 1. Planning, Design and Fabrication a. Create a layout plan (digital or sketch) for furniture, equipment, and wiring based on defined workspace needs including but not limited to desk space, storage, power, internet, seating, lighting, heating and cooling. b. Measure interior dimensions of the van. c. Check weight limits and payload capacity. d. Fabrication of a workable space for 2 to 3 users in the rear of the van, separate from the driving compartment of the vehicle 2. Electrical and Power Setup a. Install insulation and vapor barrier. b. Add wiring for outlets, lights, and devices. c. Install power system: d. Shore power connection e. Add LED lighting (ceiling, task, ambient). f. Mount Power outlets 3. Interior Build a. Install Flooring b. Build and install custom built in furniture c. Add seating solutions for workstations d. Add monitor and desktop mounts, including any necessary hardware for computer mounting e. Add wall panels f. Create compartment for network gear including but not limited to network switches, routers and cabling g. Custom cable run from workstations to network compartment 4. Mechanical and Safety a. Install heating and cooling b. Add climate control c. Include fire suppression system d. Installation of HVAC system CONSTRAINTS • All services must be executed at the Contractor’s secure facility. • The contractor must be located within the National Capital Region. Evaluation criteria for assessment of statement of capabilities (minimum essential requirements) Any interested supplier must demonstrate in their statement of capabilities that it meets the following requirements: • Maintains in-house engineering, design, fabrication, welding, electrical, and occupational health and safety capabilities at its facility, enabling performance of all phases of the vehicle fit-up project from design and fabrication through installation, testing, and final delivery. • Has successfully completed at least one (1) project within the last five (5) years involving the design and outfitting of a mobile vehicle, mobile command vehicle, specialty service vehicle, mobile workspace. • Possesses the capability to design and configure mobile operational workspaces, including the creation of scale layout plans that identify furniture location, storage, seating, electrical components and workstations. • Possesses the capability of installing vehicle insulation and vapor barrier systems suitable for year-round operation in -30 Degree Celsius conditions • Possesses the capability to design and install an integrated electrical distribution system, including wiring for outlets, lighting, and workspace equipment including but not limited to desk space, storage, power, internet, seating, lighting. • Demonstrates experience performing all the following services: integrating multiple vehicle systems, including electrical, HVAC, interior workspace, and safety systems into a single mobile operational platform. • Demonstrates experience delivering completed mobile operational or command vehicles for law enforcement, public safety, emergency management, military, or other government organizations. • Must be located no more than 50 Kilometres from the National Capital Region Trade agreement applicability This procurement is subject to the following trade agreement(s): Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA) Canada-Chile Free Trade Agreement (CCFTA) Canada-Colombia Free Trade Agreement Canada-Honduras Free Trade Agreement Canada-Panama Free Trade Agreement Canada-Peru Free Trade Agreement (CPFTA) Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP) Justification for pre-identified supplier Battleshield Industries Limited has been identified as the proposed supplier because it possesses the specialized technical capabilities, secure facilities, and resources required to complete the conversion of a vehicle into a fully functional Mobile Operational Space (MOS) supporting RCMP COMSEC operations. The goal of this procurement is to increase operational readiness, reduce deployment times and reduce mobilisation costs for COMSEC’s mobile information processing. The project requires the in-house design, fabrication, integration, testing, and delivery of a customized mobile workspace incorporating electrical distribution, climate control, safety systems, custom furnishings, equipment mounting solutions, and vehicle-specific modifications. The work requires expertise across multiple disciplines and the ability to integrate these systems into a single operational platform. Battleshield Industries Limited maintains in-house engineering, design, fabrication, welding, electrical, and health and safety capabilities, enabling the company to complete all phases of the project from design through final delivery and testing. The company also possesses the specialized equipment and expertise required to manufacture custom components and modifications tailored to the vehicle and operational requirements. Battleshield has demonstrated experience designing and manufacturing specialized operational vehicles and mobile workspace solutions for Canadian law enforcement organizations, including projects involving complex vehicle integrations and customized operational environments. Market research conducted by the RCMP did not identify another supplier within the National Capital Region possessing the same combination of in-house vehicle integration, engineering, fabrication, electrical, and testing capabilities required to perform the full scope of work as a single-source solution. Due to the operational nature of the fitted vehicle, the RCMP requires the ability to obtain maintenance, repairs, warranty work, inspections, adjustments, and other post-installation support within a short timeframe to ensure continued operational readiness. A location within the prescribed distance from RCMP National Headquarters allows the vehicle to be transported to and from the Contractor's facility efficiently, minimizing vehicle downtime and the impact on operational availability. Exclusions and /or Limited tendering reasons The following exception(s) to the Government Contracts Regulations is (are) invoked for this procurement under subsection 6(d) - "only one person is capable of performing the work. Limited Tendering procedures as tracked under internal CAP Code 71 (iii), due to an absence of competition for technical reasons. This process is compliant with the following trade agreement provisions: CFTA Article 513(1)(b)(iii), CPTPP Article 15.10(1)(b)(iii), Canada-Chile FTA Article kbis-09(1)(b), Canada-Columbia FTA Article 1409 (1)(b)(iii), Canada-Honduras FTA Article 17.11(2)

title: Ft. Lee Obstacle Course Construction
description: This is a pre-solicitation notice. Neither bids nor proposals are expected from contractors at this time. The actual solicitation is expected to be released approximately during the month of October 2026. The drawing and specification package will be included with the solicitation. Project Description: The purpose of this project is to construct a Confidence Obstacle Course (CFOC) and sheltered bleacher area with lightning protection. The CFOC will consist of twenty-four obstacle stations. Directional and obstacle signage will be provided to guide soldiers through the entire course. A 10ft maneuver trail between obstacles will be provided to support training or emergency vehicle movement through the course, to include the ability to bypass an obstacle on one side. A Tactical Assembly Area (TAA) of roughly half of an acre will be cleared in the center of the course and an entrance trail from TA-27 will be constructed. Gravel and fill dirt will be added to provide drainage away from the course and create a flat surface for all cleared areas. Facilities will be designed to a minimum life of 40 years in accordance with DoD's Unified Facilities Criteria (UFC 1-200-02) including energy efficiencies, building envelope and integrated building systems performance.

title: Freedom Connection Natural Gas Pipeline
description: ********************************************************************************** This amendment is to update the response date to 10:00 AM (AST) Thursday, 8 October 2026. ********************************************************************************** SOURCES SOUGHT - REQUEST FOR INFORMATION FREEDOM CONNECTION NATURAL GAS PIPELINE THIS NOTICE IS FOR MARKET RESEARCH PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP) OR INVITATION FOR BID. This announcement seeks information from industry which will be used for preliminary planning purposes. This is not a solicitation for proposals, and no contract will be awarded from this synopsis. No solicitation, specifications or drawings are available at this time. 1.0 Introduction and Purpose The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Latin America and Caribbean District (SAA) is conducting market research for the construction of the Freedom Connection Natural Gas Pipeline in Puerto Rico. The results of this market research will help determine the final procurement strategy. USACE-SAA is issuing this follow up Request for Information due to changes in the design, scope of work and acquisition strategy. This request is to gain knowledge of interest, capabilities, and qualifications of Small Business concerns, certified HUBZone, 8(a), Woman-Owned Small Businesses, Economically Disadvantaged Woman-Owned Small Business, Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Business or Veteran-Owned Small Business. The responses or submissions will be used for informational and planning purposes only and do not constitute a commitment by the Government. The Government will not pay for any information submitted, and respondents will not be notified of the results. Submission or responses to this request for information is not a prerequisite for any potential future offerings. 2.0 Background The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) is funding the Freedom Connection Project. The objective is to enhance the resilience of Puerto Rico�s northern power grid by improving fuel infrastructure. This project involves constructing an approximately 4.2-mile, 20-inch diameter natural gas pipeline to supply the Palo Seco Power Plant from the existing San Juan liquid natural gas (LNG) terminal. SAA anticipates soliciting and awarding one (1) design-bid-build solicitation in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Parts 15 and 36. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 237120 - Oil and Gas Pipeline and Related Structures Construction. The small business size standard for this NAICS code is US $45 million. The estimated magnitude of construction is between $25,000,000 and $100,000,000. Anticipated award date is in the second quarter of Fiscal Year 2027. Performance Period is 365 calendar days from NTP. 3.0 Scope of Work The scope of work includes all integrated procurement, labor, equipment, and services required to construct and commission the new pipeline based on a forthcoming final engineering design. Core responsibilities include: � Materials Procurement: Procure all necessary items, including long-lead items such as 20� steel pipe, valves, fittings, and instrumentation, ensuring compliance with the final design and industry standards. � Site Work: Prepare access roads and rights-of-way, and perform site clearing, grading, and stabilization. � Pipeline Installation: Execute all installation activities, including: Trenchless methods (e.g., Horizontal Directional Drilling - HDD). Open trench cut-and-cover installation. Pre-fabrication of materials. Pipeline welding, non-destructive testing (NDT), and inspection. Application of protective external coatings. Above-grade pipeline installation, potentially requiring more than 50 feet deep concrete piles. � Facilities Construction: Build all standalone facilities, including mainline block-valve stations and pig launcher/receiver stations, including electrical and instrumentation. � Delegated Design: Manage and execute any potentially delegated design elements (e.g., temporary works, trench shoring, specialized HDD drill profiles, or structural supports), including coordination with and sealing by licensed Professional Engineers. � Testing and Commissioning: Perform hydrostatic pressure testing, leak detection, and all pre-startup commissioning protocols. � Restoration and Handover: Restore all disturbed areas and formally transfer the completed pipeline and facilities to the owner/operator. 4.0 Requested Information for Capability Statement Interested firms must submit a capability statement (limited to 10 pages) that addresses the following. Responses should be tailored to demonstrate the firm's ability to successfully manage and execute this integrated procurement and construction project. Corporate Information & Experience 1. Company Profile: Provide your firm's name, address, point of contact (POC), CAGE Code, and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI). 2. Business Category: Specify your firm's socioeconomic status (e.g., Small Business, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), HUBZone, 8(a), Woman-Owned Small Business). 3. Bonding Capacity: Include documentation from your bonding company showing current single and aggregate performance and payment bond limits. 4. Project Experience: Interested construction firms may provide no more than three (3) example projects where the interested firm served as the prime contractor. Each project must include the name, title, project role, e-mail address, and telephone number of at least one reference. References may be used to verify project size, scope, dollar value, percentages and quality of performance. Example projects must be of similar size and scope. Projects similar in scope to this project include: Natural gas pipeline project of similar magnitude and complexity where your firm was responsible for both materials� procurement and construction. Civil projects involving trenchless technologies like HDD, and work in dense urban or environmentally sensitive areas. Each project must comprise of detailed scope of the work, performance timeline, dollar value, customer name. Construction of pipelines of more than 1 mile in length including trenchless pipeline installation, including horizontal directional drilling, jack and bore, and other trenchless technologies. 5.0 Submission Instructions � Deadline: Responses must be submitted via email no later than 10:00 AM (AST), Tuesday, 24 September 2026. � Email To: Angel.J.Martinez@usace.army.mil and Meranda.R.Booth@usace.army.mil. � Format: No hardcopy or facsimile submissions will be accepted.
